1 · Executive summary

Mental model (one line): retrieve grounded tenant context → reason over it with Claude → answer with citations; if the context isn't loaded, fall back to Claude's general expertise, clearly labeled — never fabricate.

Plain English: Nexus does not "memorize" your company. Every time you ask, it looks up your tenant's facts and patterns from a database + a search index, hands those to Claude as reading material, and Claude writes the answer citing them. If the lookup finds nothing, it says so instead of guessing.
Under the hood: The orchestrator is askIntelligence() (src/lib/intelligence/ask/index.ts) — an async generator emitting classified → sources → delta → followups → done. Reasoning is Anthropic/Claude only via the audited egress client (getAuditedAnthropicClient, src/lib/agent/stream.ts); provider is proven in ai_egress_audit.

What it knows today (post 2026-06-07 restore): decision/treasury patterns (Lakeshore strong) and the CXO fact layer — org, current data/analytics stack, systems, vendors, contracts, initiatives — now live in Azure and verified answerable (e.g. Meridian's Epic stack + $28.5M Epic contract; Lakeshore's named execs). Remaining gaps are specific inputs (e.g. Meridian has no named-executive roster, KPI registers are thin) — "add this file" tasks (§8.2), not a layer-wide absence. When a specific fact isn't loaded, it says "not loaded" rather than inventing.

3 · Ingestion pipeline: parse → chunk → registry → db → graph → index

flowchart LR U[Doc upload
CSV/PDF/XLSX] --> B[Azure Blob
staging] B --> P[Parse / extract] P --> SF[(enterprise_context
_source_files)] SF --> R[(records)] R --> C[(chunks)] C --> E[Embeddings
vector] R --> F[(facts
structured)] R --> G[(intelligence_
graph_edges)] E --> IDX[(Azure AI Search
tenant-context-v1)] F --> IDX C --> Q[(chunk_queue)]
Plain English: A document is uploaded, saved, and read. It's split into small passages ("chunks"), turned into structured "facts," linked into a relationship "graph," and converted into math vectors so it's searchable by meaning. Each of those is a separate step — "uploaded" is not "searchable."
Under the hood: Governed Admin bulk loader → Blob → parse → enterprise_context_source_files (lineage) → enterprise_context_records → enterprise_context_chunks (+ chunk_queue) → embeddings (OpenAI/Azure Foundry, an allowlisted non-reasoning utility) → enterprise_context_facts → intelligence_graph_edges → Azure AI Search index tenant-context-v1. Per AGENTS.md "Context ingestion truth standard," each state is reported separately — "loaded" ≠ "committed + retrievable."

Current reality (post 2026-06-07 restore): this pipeline's enterprise_context_* outputs are now present in Azure abarva_control (restored from the final backup blob; records 3,503 · facts 38,640 · chunks 15,847) and the Azure Search index tenant-context-v1 was rebuilt per tenant. The corpus/genome/graph tables remain present too.

4 · How Sentinel/Nexus are "made aware" at request time

flowchart TD Q[User question] --> T[Tenant resolve
active-client + aliases + RLS] T --> CL[Intent classify
Claude · classifier.ts] CL --> RET{Multi-retriever fan-out} RET --> R1[enterprise facts] RET --> R2[technology] RET --> R3[structured] RET --> R4[graph · genome-query-broker] RET --> R5[vector · context-broker] RET --> R6[Azure Search] R1 & R2 & R3 & R4 & R5 & R6 --> EV[Evidence assembly
+ grounding/relevance
+ namespace validation] EV --> SP[System-prompt build
module-context-contract
+ four-layer instructions] SP --> LLM[Claude synthesis
audited egress] LLM --> CIT[Answer + citations] CIT --> FU[Followups]
Plain English: The "intelligence" that makes Sentinel aware is not inside the AI model — it's the retrievers + the prompt builder. They fetch your tenant's relevant rows and paste them into the question as reading material, fresh, every single request. Nothing about your company is baked into Claude.
Under the hood: askIntelligence() resolves tenant (active-client.ts + tenant/aliases.ts, RLS-scoped), classifies intent (Claude, classifier.ts), fans out to retrievers (ask/retrievers/*, knowledge/context-broker/broker.ts for vectors, graph/retrieval.ts + genome-query-broker.ts for graph, corpus/azure-search.ts for search), validates pattern IDs against the decision's grounding namespace (pattern-grounding.ts), then synthesizer.ts injects the retrieved evidence into the system prompt (module-context-contract.ts + FOUR_LAYER_REASONING_INSTRUCTIONS) and streams Claude's answer.
QuestionAnswer
Which component holds the "awareness"?The retrievers + prompt assembler in src/lib/intelligence/ask/ — not the model.
Where is context stored / accessed?Azure Postgres (abarva_control, tenant-scoped + RLS) and Azure AI Search — read at request time.
How does binding happen in real time?Retrieved rows → an evidence block inside the per-request system prompt. Ephemeral; recomputed each call. No training/no memory of your data in the model.
What's the configuration?Env: AZURE_SEARCH_SERVICE_NAME, AZURE_CONNECTIVITY_SEARCH_INDEX_NAME, ABARVA_FEATURE_RETRIEVAL_AZURE_SEARCH_TENANTS; per-tenant clients.ai_policy (the egress gate that allows Claude).

5 · No-context fallback & the reasoning layer

flowchart TD R[Retrieval result] -->|grounded rows found| A[Answer FROM context
+ citations] R -->|nothing relevant| B[response-policy:
state what's missing] B --> C[Claude general expertise
clearly labeled
'not a loaded corpus match'] B --> D{Fabricate?} D -->|NO — fail closed| E[Refuse to invent
execs/systems/numbers]
Plain English: When the lookup finds nothing, Nexus is allowed to give general expert advice from Claude — but it must say it's general, and it must never invent your specific facts (names, systems, dollar figures). "Grounded in your data" and "the model happens to know" are deliberately kept distinct.
Under the hood: response-policy.ts governs the partial/empty-evidence path; the reasoning layer is Claude via getAuditedAnthropicClient (Anthropic-only, gated by clients.ai_policy.allowClaude). Every call is logged to ai_egress_audit (provider=anthropic). The grounding guard (pattern-grounding.ts) prevents a valid-but-off-namespace pattern ID from being cited.
Real caseBehavior
Lakeshore — "Kyriba modernization patterns?"FULLY_ANSWERABLE — 8 grounded sources (real treasury patterns), cited.
Meridian — "our analytics stack / vendors?" (post-restore)ANSWERABLE — grounded: "Epic Cogito ($3.4M/yr) on Epic Clarity + Caboodle"; "Epic contract $28.5M, renewal Jan 2026."
Meridian — "who is our CFO?" (no roster loaded)NOT_LOADED — refused to name (Meridian has no exec roster) — correct, honest.

6 · End-to-end worked examples

(a) Grounded hit — Lakeshore Kyriba

  1. Tenant resolved → Lakeshore (RLS-scoped).
  2. Intent classify (Claude) → treasury/decision-pattern.
  3. Retrievers fetch real genome LSH-TMS + corpus treasury patterns (e.g. "Kyriba-to-bank cutover dual-run", "Daily cash position originates in Kyriba").
  4. Grounding namespace = treasury → validates the cited IDs belong there.
  5. Claude synthesizes an answer citing 8 sources; followups offered.

(b) Specific input not loaded — Meridian "Who is our CFO?"

  1. Retrievers query enterprise_context_facts (now present in Azure) → relevant facts exist (CMDB, vendors, org), but no named-executive roster was ever loaded for Meridian → 0 roster evidence.
  2. response-policy → state the gap; reasoning layer must not fabricate.
  3. Answer: "the exec bench isn't in the loaded tenant data — I won't guess." (Correct — and the fix is to add executives.csv, §8.2.)

(c) Cross-namespace guard — why PAT-LSH-D18-00479 ≠ Kyriba

  1. PAT-LSH-D18-00479 is a real procurement pattern in corpus_patterns — but a different namespace than the treasury card's grounding set (genome/LSH-TMS).
  2. pattern-grounding.ts rejects it for the Kyriba card even though the ID is valid elsewhere — preventing a confident-but-wrong citation.

flowchart LR BR[Browser

flowchart LR CORP[Corpus / Context
what we know] --- RET[Retrieval

Plain English (the RAG triangle): three parts working together — what we know (corpus + your context), retrieval (finding the right bits for this question), and the LLM (reasoning over those bits into an answer). Weakness in any corner shows up as a weak answer. Today our weak corner is the "context" side for fact questions.
Under the hood: Runtime is Azure Container Apps (no Vercel); data plane is Azure private Postgres + Azure AI Search; reasoning is Anthropic-only. Auth = Clerk; tenant scoping + RLS enforce isolation.

8 · How to train / improve Sentinel & Nexus (the best-in-class process)

Key reframe: "training" here is not fine-tuning Claude's brain. It is a repeatable loop of (1) load the right data → (2) make retrieval find it → (3) tune the prompt → (4) measure with a question battery → (5) fix the gaps. Base-model fine-tuning is almost never the first move; better data + better retrieval wins.

flowchart LR L[1 · Load substrate
per dimension] --> RT[2 · Retrieval
embeddings · recall@k] RT --> PR[3 · Prompt/instructions] PR --> EV[4 · Question battery
golden-QA + grading] EV --> FX[5 · Fix gaps
+ feedback] FX --> L

8.3 · How to make it available (the governed path)

  1. Upload via the Admin bulk/zip loader → Azure Blob staging (lineage in enterprise_context_source_files).
  2. Parse/extract → records → chunks (with source file/page/row citations).
  3. Commit facts (structured) / review-queue (document-derived low-confidence).
  4. Embed chunks (vector) and refresh the Azure AI Search index (tenant-context-v1).
  5. Prove retrieval: signed-in question returns the new evidence, cited. Only then is it "available."

Each state is reported separately — "uploaded" ≠ "committed" ≠ "retrievable." A dimension is "best-in-class ready" only when step 5 passes.

8.4 · The question battery — how many tests per topic

Define a golden-QA set per dimension with a known correct answer derived from the loaded data (the "golden key"). Recommended cadence:

Per dimensionCountPurpose
Positive (should answer + cite)6Confirm grounded retrieval + correct synthesis
Partial (some evidence)2Confirm "here's what's known, here's the gap"
Negative (not loaded)2Confirm it refuses to fabricate
Per-dimension total10

~24 dimensions → ~240 golden questions per client, plus ~2 tenant-isolation probes per dimension on a sample (ask Meridian's question scoped as Lakeshore → must return zero Meridian facts).

MetricWhat it measuresBest-in-class threshold
recall@5Was the gold evidence in the top 5 retrieved?≥ 0.90
citation-support rateDo cited sources actually back each claim?≥ 0.95
hallucination rate (negatives)Did it invent facts when none were loaded?0 (hard gate)
answer completenessDoes the answer cover the golden key?≥ 0.85
tenant-leakageAny cross-tenant facts/citations?0 (hard gate)

Cadence: per-ingest smoke (1–2 questions/dimension), nightly full battery (~240), and a pre-release gate (battery must pass thresholds). Reuse the harnesses (src/__tests__/atlas-eval, scripts/qa/agent-grounding-runner.ts) and the headless askIntelligence operator-job runner; capture outcomes to outcome_pattern_feedback.

8.5 · Maturity model (definition of best-in-class)

LevelState
L0 AbsentDimension not loaded → NOT_LOADED (Meridian fact layer today)
L1 LoadedCommitted to Azure facts/chunks, embedded + indexed
L2 Retrievablerecall@5 ≥ 0.90 on the golden set
L3 Answerablecompleteness ≥ 0.85, citation-support ≥ 0.95, 0 hallucination
L4 Best-in-classL3 + benchmarked to function-pack depth + monitored nightly + feedback-improving
Plain English: "Trained well" = every topic reaches Level 3+: the data is loaded, the lookup reliably finds it, the answer is complete and cited, and it never makes things up — and we prove it with ~10 test questions per topic, every night.

9 · Glossary

RAGRetrieval-Augmented Generation — look up relevant facts, then let the LLM write using them.
EmbeddingA passage turned into numbers so similar meanings sit near each other for search.
ChunkA small slice of a document, sized for retrieval.
Vector indexA search engine over embeddings (Azure AI Search here).
GroundingTying an answer to real retrieved evidence (and the right namespace).
CitationThe specific source rows an answer points to.
Reasoning layerThe LLM (Claude) that reasons over the evidence into prose.
Corpus vs genomeCorpus = client/decision patterns (corpus_patterns); genome = the broad industry pattern library (genome_patterns).
Tenant scopingEvery read is filtered to one client (tenant_key/client_id + RLS) so no cross-tenant leakage.
